newsitem.title: CHILE: Los Pelambres to start digging copper in mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Los Pelambres to start digging copper in mid-1997.

text.p: Owners of Los Pelambres, one of the world's largest copper deposits, will break ground on the 260,000-tonne-a-year mine about the middle of this year and plan to finish it in 1999, a top company official said.

Work on the mine will follow a reshuffling of its ownership. Antofagasta Holdings Plc signed a letter of intent this week to sell 40 percent of the project to two Japanese consortia for a price they won't disclose.
"Engineering work is underway and construction should start about mid-year," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

Nestled in a remote area of the Andes next to the Argentine border, the mine will produce 260,000 tonnes of copper a year in 750,000 tonnes of concentrates, up from an original plan of 230,000 tonnes a year, said the official.
The new plan puts it well into the big leagues of Chilean copper mining and means it will likely be Chile's third largest pit in the year 2000 -- after Escondida, Chuquicamata and Collahuasi.
"This is the first major mine to be built by a private Chilean company and it's also the largest shareholding to be taken by Japanese companies," in the Chilean copper industry, said the official.

The letter of intent calls for Antofagasta to yield a combined 40 percent of the mine's equity to a consortium of Nippon Mining & Metals Co Ltd, Marubeni Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd and another consortium of Mitsubishi Corp and Mitsubishi Materials Corp.
The deal, expected to be closed by mid-1997, will give Japanese copper investors their third major stake in Chile.

Sumitomo Corp and Sumitomo Metal Mining own 20 percent of Phelps Dodge's two-year-old Candelaria mine, and Falconbridge and Minorco SA last year ceded 12 percent of their massive Collahuasi project to a Mitsui-Nippon consortium.
Antofagasta has no plans now to bring in more partners, said the official.
"We're very happy with the shareholding as laid out in the letter of intent and we have no plans to sell more at this moment," he said.
The mine will work with a ''mainstream concentrator,'' and as at Candelaria and Collahuasi, the Japanese consortia have a guaranteed share of concentrates output under the letter of intent.
The deposit, where Antofagasta currently operates a smaller mine producing 23,000 tonnes of copper a year, is enough to dazzle any investor.

Said to be the third largest copper deposit in the world, the porphyry ore body holds 2.4 billion tonnes at an average grade of 0.63 percent, with mineable ore of 930 million tonnes at an average grade of 0.75 percent in the present project.

It lies just over the border from the Pachon deposit in Argentina. A mining agreement under negotiation by both countries could someday help cooperation between the two projects but so far there has been no formal contact, said the official.
